details: CONFIRMED by a probe on this Mac (Python 3.14.6): a script whose daemon thread loops on sys.stdin.buffer.read(4096) exits -6 both on

covers only the paths that reach finish(); main() has no try/except around the steps after line 246, so every exception path
still aborts and skips RUN.abort(). The queue item python-aborts-at-exit-in-gates-macos-shows-crash is meant to close with this
change. Rated HIGH: the brief made this a must-hold line before landing and named the fix and its test; neither is met.
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: grep -n "134|abort|SIGABRT|os.read" tests/test_gate_ssh.py tests/fake_vps.py -> no dedicated test
failing_case: The program has read the frame and started the stdin watcher (line 246); then any uncaught exception leaves main by the normal
interpreter exit, e.g. subprocess.TimeoutExpired from `podman create` (timeout=120, line 203), `podman cp` (300), `git fetch` (300),
`podman ps` (60), or ValueError from int(opts["slots"]). Now: Python 3.14 aborts (exit -6 / 134, a macOS crash report each time the
fake-host tests hit such a path) and RUN.abort() never runs, so the temporary folder and a created container stay. Should: the
process ends with a plain non-zero exit (1), no SIGABRT, and the container and the temporary folder are removed.
The brief said: "Use os.read(0, 4096) and add a test that runs the program with an open stdin pipe and a normal end and asserts
exit 0". The change instead routes the normal paths through os._exit (finish) and keeps sys.stdin.buffer.read; no dedicated test exists.
fix_hint: watch_stdin: `while os.read(0, 4096): pass` (read_frame has consumed exactly the frame from the buffered reader, so nothing is lost);
wrap main's body after RUN.tmp is set in try/except BaseException that prints relay-gate-error, calls RUN.abort() and finish(91).
Add the test the brief names (open stdin pipe, normal end, exit 0) plus one exception-path test asserting no -6.
pass_cases: 1. Run lib/relay_gate_remote.py under the fake host with stdin an open pipe and a normal end (a green gate): exit 0, no -6/134.
2. The same with an exception raised after the watcher starts (e.g. a mock raising in run_container, or a fake podman create that
outlives a patched timeout): exit code is a positive number (not -6/134), and the temporary folder RUN.tmp no longer exists.
3. Stdin closed by the Mac before the end: still the 98 path and the container removed
(test_a_lost_connection_after_the_running_line_is_a_could_not_run keeps passing).
4. The cut during podman create (test_a_cut_while_the_container_is_still_being_created_removes_it_once_created) keeps passing.

findings.summary: the brief's must-hold fix is not made: watch_stdin still reads sys.stdin.buffer, so any exit that is not os._exit (an uncaught exception) still aborts with SIGABRT on Python 3.14

details: CONFIRMED by reading (lines 162-170, 62-75): Run holds only container and tmp; build_image's Popen handle is local. The plan's F5
says "a build never runs without a slot". The systemd Linger=no backstop only kills it when the account's last session closes, which
with other gates open does not happen. Consequence on the real host PLAUSIBLE (not run). Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_gate_remote.py:71-75 abort(): podman rm -f container; rmtree tmp  (no build process)
failing_case: A watch's first build (311 s cold on this Mac; bound 3600 s for a watch) is running when the Mac sleeps or its connection drops:
stdin closes, watch_stdin calls RUN.cut_now(98) -> abort() removes RUN.tmp (the build context under it) and os._exit. The podman build
was started with start_new_session=True and is not in RUN, so it keeps running, unbounded (its communicate timeout died with the
process), holding CPU outside any slot; the slot and build locks are released, so the next gate starts a second build of the same
tag. Should: a cut kills the build's process group, as the build-limit path does (os.killpg).
fix_hint: Keep the build's pid in RUN (RUN.build = proc.pid) and in abort() os.killpg(RUN.build, SIGKILL) when set; clear it after communicate.
pass_cases: 1. Fake podman build that sleeps (build_hang); the Mac's connection is lost after the build starts (a fake ssh mode that sends SIGHUP
once the build has begun): the fake podman build process is gone within a few seconds and the build lock is free.
2. A build past build_limit_s still ends with the "still building" line and is killed
(test_a_build_runs_inside_its_slot_and_is_killed_at_its_bound keeps passing).
3. A cut during podman create still removes the created container (existing test keeps passing).
findings.summary: a cut during an image build leaves the podman build running with no bound and outside any slot (it is in its own session and RUN.abort does not know it)

details: CONFIRMED: `git rev-parse HEAD:no-such-file` prints "HEAD:no-such-file", rc 128; git() returns stdout regardless of rc. Size: 5 min.
failing_case: A repository without deps.toml (or install.sh): `git rev-parse <sha>:deps.toml` prints "<sha>:deps.toml" on stdout (exit 128) and
`git rev-parse <tip>:deps.toml` prints "<tip>:deps.toml"; they differ, so every lane gate exits 94 "the branch changes the image
recipe (deps.toml)". Should: a file absent in both is unchanged. relay has all three files today, so it does not fire now.
fix_hint: Use `rev-parse --verify -q` and map rc != 0 to "" in the blobs dict.
pass_cases: 1. Repo without deps.toml in both commits: blobs compare equal, the gate runs.
2. Branch that adds deps.toml: 94.
3. Branch that changes container/Containerfile: 94.
findings.summary: a recipe file missing from both commits counts as changed: git rev-parse echoes the unresolved argument, so mine and theirs differ whenever sha != tip

details: PLAUSIBLE race; CONFIRMED by reading that nothing clears AGAIN at start and the re-gate does not check tip != target when again.
